title: 253. Can a search put a human ELM motif on its chicken ortholog?
question: Does a search put a human ELM motif on its 1:1 chicken ortholog at the place the motif sits in the ortholog, and does kmerseek place motifs the other tools miss?
dataset: 1_303 human proteins with 2_160 ELM true-positive instances vs the chicken proteome (QfO 2020_04, 17_837 proteins); 540 motifs with a projected position on the 1:1 OMA ortholog; 266 kmerseek arms with results plus 8 comparison tools
comparison_tools: phmmer; HMMER; MMseqs2; HHblits; Foldseek; ProstT5; Reseek
result: kmerseek_best_arm_on_position_share=0.818519 [cell 8] | jackhmmer_on_position_share=0.987037 [cell 8] | foldseek_on_position_share=0.484112 [cell 8] | kmerseek_best_arm_ortholog_rank_over_10=348 [cell 20] | motifs_only_kmerseek_places=0 [cell 23] | spearman_region_mean_idf_vs_call_length_median=0.795851 [cell 32] | on_position_ratio_scaled10_vs_scaled1_median=2.023121 [cell 17] | foldseek_misses_kmerseek_places=216 [cell 26]
verdict_basis: Cell 32 shows region_mean_idf, the score that ranks kmerseek calls and cuts each list to 1_000 targets, follows call length (median Spearman 0.795851 over 266 arms); cell 20 shows the ortholog below rank 10 for 348 of 442 motifs and cell 17 shows subsampling the index doubles the share, and commit 18f5b53 changes the top-N cut to the union of region_mean_idf and region_evalue because of this.
notes: As printed, kmerseek's best arm (protein20 k=5, scaled 1) puts 81.9% of motifs on position against 96.1-98.7% for the six sequence tools, and places no motif that every comparison tool misses (cell 23); it recovers 216 of Foldseek's 276 misses, all found by sequence tools. The length effect: the list order, and so the cut to 1_000 chicken targets, favours long calls, which can push the ortholog out; scaled 10 gives 2.02 times the on-position share of scaled 1 (cell 17). Commit 18f5b53 on olgabot/kmerseek-top-targets (2026-09-29) keeps the union of the mean-IDF and E-value top N; chicken has not been rescored with it in this notebook. Seven more species are PR 72 (olgabot/elm-cover-all-species). No aligned residues are printed. jackhmmer is listed as HMMER; 'Foldseek with ProstT5' as ProstT5.
